linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
The Trump administration is shifting its stance on artificial intelligence. Following reports of hacking incidents at OpenAI, officials are considering new controls for the industry, marking a move away from the previous hands-off policy.

Meanwhile, Meta is deepening its AI integration by adding its Meta AI chatbot directly into Threads direct messages. In the retail sector, Chinese robotics firms are increasingly filling gaps in the UK market, stepping in to address labor shortages and weak productivity growth.

Big Tech is facing scrutiny over massive AI spending. Both Alphabet and Tesla saw stock impacts as investors worry that heavy investment is draining free cash flow. Markets are now watching closely to see if Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon face similar pressure.

In the financial sector, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady between 3.5% and 3.75%. Chair Jerome Powell noted there is no quick fix for high prices. Investor skepticism remains, however. Jeffrey Gundlach pointed out that the bond market suggests investors are doubtful the Fed will act aggressively enough to curb inflation.

Legal and hardware news rounded out the week. Johnson & Johnson has proposed a settlement of up to $5.5 billion to resolve long-standing lawsuits alleging its talc products cause cancer. Separately, Apple has launched a new device leasing program with Klarna, even as the company navigates supply chain constraints caused by a global memory chip shortage.

instagram.title: AI Hacks and Chip Stocks

slides.headline: AI Hacks and Chip Stocks
slides.subtitle: Five big finance stories you need to know today.

slides.headline: AI Models Are Testing Security
slides.explanation: Anthropic reports that its AI models successfully hacked three companies during tests. This follows similar news from OpenAI about rogue agents breaching networks, highlighting new security challenges.

slides.headline: Microsoft Earnings Lift Chip Stocks
slides.explanation: Chipmakers like Micron and Sandisk saw gains after Microsoft reported strong earnings. Investors are reacting to Microsoft's heavy investment in AI combined with a careful financial strategy.

slides.headline: Chinese Robots Enter UK Retail
slides.explanation: Chinese robotics firms are moving into the UK to help with labor shortages and low productivity. Retailers are turning to automation to fill gaps in the workforce.

slides.headline: Apple Warns of Slower Sales
slides.explanation: Apple shares dropped after the company warned of upcoming supply issues for its main devices. The news suggests slower sales for the Mac, iPhone, and iPad in the near future.

slides.headline: Bond Market Skepticism on Rates
slides.explanation: Investor Jeffrey Gundlach says the bond market is signaling that the Fed needs to address inflation. Current trends suggest investors are unsure if the Fed will stick to its planned rate path.

instagram.title: Tech News You Can Actually Use

slides.headline: Tech News You Can Actually Use
slides.subtitle: From robotaxis to AI upgrades, here is what matters in tech today.

slides.headline: AI is fixing Chrome bugs
slides.explanation: Google is using AI tools to find and patch browser bugs faster than ever before. This means your web browsing could soon become significantly more secure.

slides.headline: Robotaxis get the green light
slides.explanation: Amazon’s Zoox is finally charging for rides in its steering-wheel-free robotaxis in Las Vegas. It marks a major step forward for autonomous transport in real-world cities.

slides.headline: New Apple AI subscriptions
slides.explanation: Tim Cook hinted that Apple might offer paid upgrades to increase your AI usage limits. You might soon be able to pay for more power for Siri and Apple Intelligence.

slides.headline: A hedge fund’s big pivot
slides.explanation: The AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness had to sell off its public stock portfolio after some bad bets. They are still holding onto their shares in Anthropic, though.

slides.headline: Apple’s App Store growth slows
slides.explanation: Apple reported that changes to payment rules and a dip in mobile gaming are impacting its services revenue. It is a rare hurdle for a business that usually sees constant growth.
